title: Existence of a direct-image Roos object
statement: For the actual additive system direct image and a normalized reduction of an arbitrary derived object, there exist a product of the finite direct-image terms, a SfIntegralDirectImage Roos triangle, and an isomorphism from the total derived coefficient limit to its Roos object.

source.place: Construction 4.1, printed p. 21; Lemma 4.10, printed pp. 23--24; Stacks Tag 0941.

proof.text: Choose one K-injective representative of the reduced object. Apply the project derived tower-limit theorem to the sectionwise direct image, and transport its product and triangle through the canonical finite restriction/direct-image comparisons. The resulting transition is the recorded sfDirectImageTransition.

lean.statement:
theorem systemDirectImage_roosExistence
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [(integralComparisonSequenceDirectImage l E f).Additive]
    [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions (coefficientSequenceModules l E X)]
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X)
    (K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E X)) :
    let N := (integralComparisonSequenceDirectImage l E f).rightDerivedFunctor.obj
      (S.reduction.obj K)
    ∃ hprod : HasProduct (sfDirectImageTerm l E f K),
      ∃ L : @SfIntegralDirectImage l _ E _ _ _ X Y f K hprod,
        ∃ e : ((coefficientSequenceLimit l E Y).obj N ≅ L.obj), True
